newsitem.title: JAPAN: Polar Air Cargo to begin services to Japan.
newsitem.headline: Polar Air Cargo to begin services to Japan.

text.p: Japan's Transport Ministry said on Wednesday that Polar Air Cargo of the United States is expected to start cargo service to Japan following an agreement in April between Tokyo and Washington on air cargo services.
The agreement provides an expansion of business rights to more air cargo airlines on both sides.
The California-based company plans six flights a week from New York, with stops in Chicago and Anchorage, to Osaka. Of the six, three flights will fly beyond Osaka to Seoul.
Polar Air Cargo plans to use Boeing 747F jets for the flights.
The ministry did not say when the flights would begin.
Polar had earlier said that it has been tentatively awarded the new U.S.-Japan freighter route by the U.S. government.

The company said in a statement that it had proposed to operate six times a week to Osaka from eight U.S. cities, including New York (JFK), Los Angeles, Chicago, San Francisco, Atlanta, Miami, Seattle and Anchorage.
